title: The Swallow and the Other Birds
text:
In spring a swallow saw a farmer sowing seed in a field and recognized it: hemp, or in some versions flax. She gathered the other birds and warned them. That seed, she said, would grow into the plant men twist into cord and weave into the nets they use to catch birds. Now, while it lay on the ground, they should pick up every grain and eat it.

The other birds laughed at her. It was only a few seeds in the dirt, and there was plenty of other food. Why should they bother?

The seed sprouted and the plants came up green. The swallow warned them again: pull up the young shoots now, before it is too late. Again they ignored her.

The crop ripened and was harvested, and from its fibers men made cords and nets. Soon birds that had mocked the swallow were being caught in snares made from that very field. The swallow left the open country and went to live near people's houses, under their eaves, where she was safe. The other birds stayed in the fields and were trapped.
lesson: Small threats are cheapest to deal with when they first appear. Waiting until a danger is fully grown means facing it when it is strongest.
caveat: Versions differ on the bird and the plant: some give the warning to an owl or name flax instead of hemp.
